title: Customer lifetime totals
prompt: Using a CTE, return customer_id, full_name, lifetime_cents (sum of payments.amount_cents) for customers with at least one payment. Sort by lifetime_cents descending, then customer_id.
hints: Payments link to customers through orders.
Aggregate per customer inside the CTE, then join names on afterwards.
WITH paid AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(p.amount_cents) ... GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT ...

title: Items vs payments without fan-out
prompt: For paid orders, return order_id, items_cents (sum of quantity × unit_price_cents) and paid_cents (sum of payment amounts, 0 if none), sorted by order_id. Joining items and payments directly multiplies rows; aggregate each side first.
hints: An order with 2 lines and 1 payment becomes 2 rows when you join both, so the payment counts twice.
Pre-aggregate order_items per order and payments per order, then join the two summaries.
Two CTEs (items, paid) and a LEFT JOIN with COALESCE(paid.paid_cents, 0).

title: Above-average prices
prompt: Return sku, unit_price_cents for products priced above the average price of all products. Sort by price descending, then sku.
hints: The average is one value computed from the whole table.
A scalar subquery can sit on the right of a comparison.
WHERE unit_price_cents > (SELECT AVG(unit_price_cents) FROM products)

title: Customers who paid
prompt: Using EXISTS, return customer_id, full_name for customers with at least one paid order, sorted by customer_id.
hints: EXISTS asks a yes/no question per outer row.
The subquery must refer to the outer customer (it is correlated).
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND ...)

title: Products nobody paid for
prompt: Using NOT EXISTS, return sku, product_name for products that do not appear in any paid order, sorted by sku.
hints: A product can appear in pending or cancelled orders and still qualify.
The subquery needs order_items joined to orders to see the status.
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ... WHERE i.product_id = p.product_id AND o.status = 'paid')

title: Pending and paid
prompt: Using INTERSECT, return customer_id for customers who have both a pending order and a paid order, sorted by customer_id.
hints: Build two lists of customer IDs and keep only those in both.
INTERSECT works on whole result rows, so select only customer_id.
SELECT customer_id ... 'pending' INTERSECT SELECT customer_id ... 'paid' ORDER BY customer_id;

title: Two-stage order report
prompt: Stage 1: total each paid order (sum of quantity × unit_price_cents). Stage 2: per customer, return customer_id, paid_orders (count) and avg_order_cents (average order total rounded to the nearest cent). Sort by customer_id.
hints: Averaging order lines directly gives the wrong answer: you need the average of order totals.
The first CTE should produce one row per paid order.
WITH order_totals AS (... GROUP BY o.order_id, o.customer_id) SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*), ROUND(AVG(total_cents)) ...

title: Status counts in one row
prompt: Return one row with paid_count, pending_count, cancelled_count using conditional aggregation over orders.
hints: One scan of orders, three counters.
A CASE expression can turn each row into 1 or 0 for a given status.
SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'paid' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS paid_count, ...

title: Price bands
prompt: Return sku, price_band for every product, where price_band is 'budget' below 1000 cents, 'standard' from 1000 to 9999, and 'premium' from 10000 up. Sort by sku.
hints: CASE checks its WHEN branches top to bottom and stops at the first match.
Order the conditions from lowest to highest threshold.
CASE WHEN unit_price_cents < 1000 THEN 'budget' WHEN ... ELSE 'premium' END

title: Salary rank within team
prompt: Return team_name, full_name, salary_rank where salary_rank is RANK() by salary (highest = 1) within each team. Sort by team_name, salary_rank, full_name.
hints: A window function ranks rows without collapsing them.
PARTITION BY restarts the ranking for each team.
RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY e.team_id ORDER BY e.salary_cents DESC)

title: Top two earners per team
prompt: Return team_name, full_name, salary_cents for the two highest-paid employees of each team (use ROW_NUMBER; break salary ties by employee_id). Sort by team_name, then salary descending.
hints: You cannot filter on a window function in the same SELECT's WHERE.
Number rows per team in a CTE, then filter the CTE.
WITH ranked AS (SELECT ..., ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY team_id ORDER BY salary_cents DESC, employee_id) AS rn ...) ... WHERE rn <= 2

title: Previous order date
prompt: Return customer_id, order_id, ordered_at, previous_ordered_at (the same customer's previous order date, NULL for their first order). Sort by customer_id, ordered_at, order_id.
hints: LAG looks one row back inside a window.
Each customer is a separate history.
LAG(ordered_at) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at, order_id)

title: Running revenue by month
prompt: Group payments by month of paid_at (format YYYY-MM). Return month, revenue_cents and running_cents (cumulative revenue up to and including that month). Sort by month.
hints: First reduce payments to one row per month.
A running total is SUM() OVER an ordered window.
WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', paid_at) AS month, SUM(...) ... GROUP BY month) SELECT ..., SUM(revenue_cents) OVER (ORDER BY month)

title: Signup month
prompt: Return customer_id, signup_month (joined_at formatted as YYYY-MM) for every customer, sorted by customer_id.
hints: SQLite stores these dates as ISO text.
strftime formats a date; %Y is the year and %m the month.
strftime('%Y-%m', joined_at)

title: Orders long after signup
prompt: Return order_id, customer_id, days_after_signup (whole days between joined_at and ordered_at, as an integer) for orders placed more than 7 days after the customer joined. Sort by order_id.
hints: Subtracting two date strings does not give days.
julianday() turns a date into a day number you can subtract.
CAST(julianday(o.ordered_at) - julianday(c.joined_at) AS INTEGER)

title: UNION vs UNION ALL
prompt: Combine customer_id from pending orders with customer_id from paid orders. Return one row with union_rows (row count using UNION) and union_all_rows (row count using UNION ALL).
hints: UNION removes duplicate rows; UNION ALL keeps them.
Wrap each combined query in a subquery and count its rows.
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (... UNION ...)) AS union_rows, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (... UNION ALL ...)) AS union_all_rows;

title: A reusable view
prompt: Create a view named paid_customer_totals with columns customer_id and lifetime_cents: the sum of payments per customer, for customers with payments. The checker reads the view and confirms it is a view, not a table.
verify: SELECT customer_id, lifetime_cents FROM paid_customer_totals ORDER BY customer_id
SELECT type FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'paid_customer_totals'
hints: A view is a saved SELECT with a name.
Start from your PI01 aggregation without the names.
CREATE VIEW paid_customer_totals AS SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(p.amount_cents) AS lifetime_cents ...

title: Undo part of a transaction
prompt: In one transaction: set product 1's price to 0, then undo only that change with a savepoint, then set product 2's price to 300 and commit. The checker reads both prices afterwards.
verify: SELECT product_id, unit_price_cents FROM products WHERE product_id IN (1, 2) ORDER BY product_id
hints: The savepoint must be created before the change you want to undo.
ROLLBACK TO name undoes back to the savepoint but keeps the transaction open.
BEGIN; SAVEPOINT s; UPDATE ...; ROLLBACK TO s; RELEASE s; UPDATE ...; COMMIT;

title: No paid order yet
prompt: Return customer_id, full_name for customers with no paid order, including customers with no orders at all. Sort by customer_id.
hints: Joining to orders and filtering status <> 'paid' keeps customers who also have a paid order.
Ask the question the other way round: does a paid order exist for this customer?
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.status = 'paid')

title: Monthly revenue dashboard
prompt: Using order lines of paid orders, group by month of ordered_at (YYYY-MM). Return month, revenue_cents and change_cents (this month minus the previous month; NULL for the first month). Sort by month.
hints: Build monthly totals first, then compare each month with the one before.
LAG(value) returns NULL on the first row, and NULL minus anything is NULL.
revenue_cents - LAG(revenue_cents) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS change_cents

title: Lines and payments per order
prompt: For paid orders, return order_id, line_count (number of order lines) and payment_count (number of payments, 0 if none), sorted by order_id. Count each table separately so neither count is multiplied by the other.
hints: Joining items and payments together makes both counts equal to lines × payments.
Count lines per order and payments per order in two separate summaries.
Two pre-aggregated subqueries or CTEs, joined to orders; COALESCE the payment count.

title: Paid orders that don't add up
prompt: Return order_id, items_cents, paid_cents (0 if no payment) for paid orders whose payment total differs from their item total, sorted by order_id. (The course data has none; the edge fixture has one.)
hints: Build the per-order comparison from PI02 first.
Then keep only rows where the two totals differ.
WHERE o.status = 'paid' AND items.items_cents <> COALESCE(paid.paid_cents, 0)

title: Above their team's average
prompt: Return full_name, team_id, salary_cents for employees paid more than the average salary of their own team, sorted by team_id, then salary descending.
hints: Each employee is compared with a different average.
A correlated scalar subquery can compute the average of the outer row's team.
WHERE e.salary_cents > (SELECT AVG(x.salary_cents) FROM employees x WHERE x.team_id = e.team_id)

title: Products sold in paid orders
prompt: Using IN with a subquery, return sku, product_name for products that appear in at least one paid order, sorted by sku.
hints: The subquery returns a list of product IDs.
It needs order_items joined to orders to see the status.
WHERE product_id IN (SELECT i.product_id FROM order_items i JOIN orders o ... WHERE o.status = 'paid')

title: Bigger teams
prompt: Using a derived table (a subquery in FROM), return team_name, headcount for teams with at least two employees, sorted by team_name.
hints: Count per team inside the subquery.
Outside it, the count is an ordinary column you can filter with WHERE.
FROM (SELECT team_id, COUNT(*) AS headcount ... GROUP BY team_id) AS s JOIN teams t ...

title: Teams without employees
prompt: Using NOT EXISTS, return team_id, team_name for teams with no employees, sorted by team_id.
hints: The course data has none; the edge fixture adds one.
Correlate the subquery with the outer team.
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM employees e WHERE e.team_id = t.team_id)

title: Quick first orders
prompt: Return customer_id, full_name for customers who placed any order within 30 days of joining (at most 30 days after joined_at), sorted by customer_id.
hints: A customer with several quick orders appears once.
julianday() lets you subtract dates in days.
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND julianday(o.ordered_at) - julianday(c.joined_at) <= 30)

title: Months above average
prompt: With a CTE of monthly paid revenue (lines of paid orders, month of ordered_at as YYYY-MM), return month, revenue_cents for months whose revenue is above the average month. Sort by month.
hints: The monthly totals are needed twice: once to list, once to average.
A CTE can be referenced from a subquery in the same statement.
WITH monthly AS (...) SELECT ... FROM monthly WHERE revenue_cents > (SELECT AVG(revenue_cents) FROM monthly)

title: Big spenders
prompt: Using CTEs, return customer_id, full_name, revenue_cents (paid order lines) for customers whose paid revenue is at least 15000 cents, sorted by revenue_cents descending, then customer_id.
hints: Stage 1: revenue per customer. Stage 2: names and the threshold.
Filter the aggregated value in the second stage with an ordinary WHERE.
WITH revenue AS (... GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT ... FROM revenue r JOIN customers c ... WHERE r.revenue_cents >= 15000

title: Payment method pivot
prompt: Return month (paid_at as YYYY-MM), card_cents, transfer_cents, cash_cents (0 when a method has no payments that month), sorted by month.
hints: One output column per payment method.
SUM a CASE that returns the amount for one method and 0 otherwise.
SUM(CASE WHEN method = 'card' THEN amount_cents ELSE 0 END) AS card_cents, ...

title: High earners per team
prompt: Return team_id, staff (number of employees) and high_earners (employees earning more than 8000000 cents) for each team that has employees, sorted by team_id.
hints: Two counts per team: all rows, and only some rows.
A CASE inside SUM counts the rows that match a condition.
SUM(CASE WHEN salary_cents > 8000000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS high_earners

title: Work queue order
prompt: Return order_id, status for every order, sorted pending first, then paid, then cancelled, and by order_id within each status.
hints: Alphabetical order is cancelled, paid, pending, which is not what you want.
ORDER BY can sort by a CASE expression that maps each status to a number.
ORDER BY CASE status WHEN 'pending' THEN 0 WHEN ... END, order_id

title: Share of revenue
prompt: For customers with paid revenue (lines of paid orders), return customer_id, revenue_cents and pct_of_total (their percentage of all paid revenue, rounded to 1 decimal). Sort by revenue_cents descending, then customer_id.
hints: Aggregate per customer, then compare each row with the grand total.
SUM(x) OVER () repeats the grand total on every row.
ROUND(100.0 * revenue_cents / SUM(revenue_cents) OVER (), 1)

title: Second-highest salary per team
prompt: Return team_id, full_name, salary_cents for everyone who earns their team's second-highest distinct salary (keep ties). Sort by team_id, then full_name.
hints: Ties must share a rank, and no rank may be skipped.
DENSE_RANK per team, computed in a CTE, then filtered.
DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY team_id ORDER BY salary_cents DESC) ... WHERE dr = 2

title: Priciest product per category
prompt: Return category_id, sku, unit_price_cents for the single most expensive product of each category (break price ties by sku). Sort by category_id.
hints: Exactly one row per category, even with ties.
ROW_NUMBER with a tie-breaker in the window's ORDER BY.
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category_id ORDER BY unit_price_cents DESC, sku) ... WHERE rn = 1

title: Days since the previous order
prompt: Return customer_id, order_id, days_since_previous (whole days since the same customer's previous order; NULL for their first) for every order. Sort by customer_id, ordered_at, order_id.
hints: LAG gives the previous order date within each customer.
julianday turns dates into numbers you can subtract.
CAST(julianday(ordered_at) - julianday(LAG(ordered_at) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at, order_id)) AS INTEGER)

title: Running spend per customer
prompt: For paid orders, return customer_id, order_id, total_cents (the order's line total) and running_cents (the customer's cumulative paid total up to and including this order, by ordered_at then order_id). Sort by customer_id, ordered_at, order_id.
hints: First one row per paid order with its total.
A running total restarts per customer: PARTITION BY.
SUM(total_cents) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY ordered_at, order_id)

title: Three-month moving average
prompt: Group payments by month of paid_at (YYYY-MM). Return month and moving_avg_3: the average of this month's and up to two previous months' received amounts, rounded to a whole number. Sort by month.
hints: One row per month first.
A bounded window frame limits which rows the average sees.
AVG(revenue_cents) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)

title: Orders per quarter
prompt: Return quarter (text like '2026-Q1') and orders (count of orders, any status) per quarter of ordered_at. Sort by quarter.
hints: The quarter number comes from the month.
(month + 2) / 3 with integer division maps 1–3 to 1, 4–6 to 2…
strftime('%Y', d) || '-Q' || ((CAST(strftime('%m', d) AS INTEGER) + 2) / 3)

title: Orders by weekday
prompt: Return weekday (0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday, as an integer) and orders (count, any status) for weekdays that have orders. Sort by weekday.
hints: strftime has a format code for the day of the week.
strftime returns text; the prompt asks for an integer.
CAST(strftime('%w', ordered_at) AS INTEGER) AS weekday

title: Orders in June
prompt: Return order_id, ordered_at for orders placed in June 2026, using a half-open date range. Sort by ordered_at, then order_id.
hints: Start of the month inclusive, start of the next month exclusive.
ISO dates compare correctly as text.
WHERE ordered_at >= '2026-06-01' AND ordered_at < '2026-07-01'

title: Email local parts
prompt: Return customer_id and local_part (the part of the email before '@') for every customer, sorted by customer_id.
hints: Find the position of '@' first.
SUBSTR(text, start, length): the length is the position of '@' minus one.
SUBSTR(email, 1, INSTR(email, '@') - 1)

title: Pending or paid by transfer
prompt: Using UNION, return customer_id for customers who have a pending order or who paid at least once by transfer, each once, sorted by customer_id.
hints: Two lists of customer IDs combined, without duplicates.
Transfer payments reach customers through orders.
SELECT customer_id ... 'pending' UNION SELECT o.customer_id FROM payments p JOIN orders o ... WHERE p.method = 'transfer'

title: Products in pending and paid orders
prompt: Using INTERSECT, return product_id for products that appear both in a pending order and in a paid order, sorted by product_id.
hints: Build both product lists from order_items joined to orders.
INTERSECT keeps values present in both.
SELECT i.product_id ... 'pending' INTERSECT SELECT i.product_id ... 'paid'

title: Ordered but never paid
prompt: Using EXCEPT, return customer_id for customers who placed at least one order but never had a paid order, sorted by customer_id.
hints: Everyone who ordered, minus everyone who paid.
EXCEPT removes the second list from the first.
SELECT customer_id FROM orders EXCEPT SELECT ... WHERE status = ...

title: Monthly revenue view
prompt: Create a view monthly_paid_revenue with columns month (ordered_at as YYYY-MM) and revenue_cents (lines of paid orders). The checker reads it, confirms it is a view, then adds a paid sale and reads it again.
verify: SELECT month, revenue_cents FROM monthly_paid_revenue ORDER BY month
SELECT type FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'monthly_paid_revenue'
hints: A view is recomputed when read, so the new sale must show up.
CREATE VIEW name AS followed by your monthly SELECT.
CREATE VIEW monthly_paid_revenue AS SELECT strftime('%Y-%m', o.ordered_at) AS month, SUM(...) AS revenue_cents ...

title: Record a sale atomically
prompt: In one transaction, record order 300 for customer 2 on '2026-09-01' with status 'paid', one line of product 3 (quantity 2 at 4900 cents), and payment 300 of 9800 cents by card on '2026-09-01'. Commit.
verify: SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.status, SUM(i.quantity * i.unit_price_cents) FROM orders o JOIN order_items i ON i.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.order_id = 300 GROUP BY o.order_id
SELECT payment_id, order_id, amount_cents, method, paid_at FROM payments WHERE payment_id = 300
hints: The order must exist before its line and payment (foreign keys).
Wrap the three inserts between BEGIN and COMMIT.
BEGIN; INSERT INTO orders ...; INSERT INTO order_items ...; INSERT INTO payments ...; COMMIT;
